A fresh agent costs more than it looks. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

Stock, orders and invoices from three plain text files. Python 3.9+, standard library only.

```
pip install .
```

installs the importable `stockroom` package and the `stockroom` command (`python -m stockroom` works too).

## Files

The files live in the current folder, or the folder given with `--dir DIR` (accepted anywhere on the line):
`catalog.txt` (`SKU | name | price | reorder [| tax]`), `movements.txt` (`DATE SKU QUANTITY [NOTE]`)
and `orders.txt` (`ORDER DATE CUSTOMER SKU*QTY,...`). Text is UTF-8, a BOM is ignored, lines end at LF or
CRLF, blank lines and `#` lines are skipped. A missing `movements.txt` or `orders.txt` is empty; a missing
`catalog.txt` is an error.

## Commands

```
stockroom stock [--json]
stockroom low [--json]
stockroom history SKU [--json]
stockroom receive DATE SKU QUANTITY [NOTE]
stockroom ship DATE SKU QUANTITY [NOTE]
stockroom quote ORDER [--json]
stockroom fulfil ORDER DATE
stockroom invoice ORDER [--json]
stockroom report [--format text|csv|json]
```

Exit status: `0` worked; `1` a data file has a mistake or the request is refused (message on stderr naming
the file and line, nothing on stdout); `2` unreadable file, bad folder, non-UTF-8, or a bad command line.

## Library

```python
import stockroom

catalog = stockroom.parse_catalog(open("catalog.txt", encoding="utf-8").read())
moves = stockroom.parse_movements(open("movements.txt", encoding="utf-8").read(), catalog)
print(stockroom.stock_levels(catalog, moves))
orders = stockroom.parse_orders(open("orders.txt", encoding="utf-8").read(), catalog)
print(stockroom.price_order(orders[0], catalog).total)
```

Mistakes raise `stockroom.ParseError` (a `ValueError` with `.line`).

Size limits: a price may be at most 1000000.00, and a quantity or reorder level at most
1000000000. Anything bigger is reported as a mistake on its line.

## Tests

python -m unittest        # or: python -m pytest
```
